description: The second set of system variables, covering command-line dialogs, selection behaviour (pick box, auto-window, cycling, preview), point display, angle and precision formats, hatch defaults, transparency, multilines, viewports, dynamic input, tooltips, highlighting, cursor, polyline and spline behaviour, explode/PEDIT defaults, layer-lock fading, grips, UCS and view state, snap/grid/polar/osnap engines, dragging, elevation, lineweight display, 3D sub-object selection, mouse-wheel zoom, shortcut menus, fillet/chamfer/offset/mirror/trim defaults and selection colours. Each entry groups the closely related variables so a whole family is documented together.

tools.name: CMDDIA
tools.description: Controls whether commands that have both a dialog and a command-line form use the dialog (1) or the command prompts (0) - it governs PLOT, QLEADER settings, and the in-place editors in older releases, and is the companion of FILEDIA for file dialogs. Scripts and Core Console jobs set both to 0 so nothing waits for a click; interactive users leave them at 1.
tools.usage:
CMDDIA = 0 (command-line prompts) | 1 (dialogs, default)
FILEDIA = 0 | 1 (file selection dialogs)
ATTDIA = 0 | 1 (attribute dialog on INSERT)

parameters.description: PLOT behaves like -PLOT; -commands are not needed.
Dialogs appear; use hyphen-prefixed commands to bypass them individually.

tools.example:
; script prelude
CMDDIA 0
FILEDIA 0
ATTDIA 0
; ... work ...
CMDDIA 1
FILEDIA 1
ATTDIA 1
tools.notes: Registry setting, so a crashed script leaves the user without dialogs - restore at the end or run the Core Console with /isolate. A tilde (~) typed at a file prompt forces the dialog even when FILEDIA is 0.

tools.name: PICKBOX
tools.description: Sets the size in pixels of the object selection target (the small square at the crosshair) used when picking objects; APERTURE is the separate, usually larger, target for object snap acquisition. Both are also set with sliders in OPTIONS > Selection and > Drafting. Too small a pick box misses thin lines on high-DPI screens; too large picks the wrong object in dense drawings.
tools.usage:
PICKBOX = 0-50 pixels (default 3; typical 5-8 on 4K displays)
APERTURE = 1-50 pixels (default 10) - object snap target box
OPTIONS > Selection > Pickbox size / OPTIONS > Drafting > Aperture size

parameters.name: PICKBOX 0
parameters.description: Selection by picking still works at the exact pixel; used by some LISP routines temporarily.

tools.example:
PICKBOX 6
APERTURE 14
tools.notes: Registry setting. PICKBOX also determines the target for ENTSEL in LISP unless the routine sets its own. Sub-object selection in 3D uses the same box.

tools.name: PICKAUTO
tools.description: Controls automatic windowing at the Select objects prompt: whether clicking in empty space starts a window/crossing selection, and (bit values in 2015+) whether a click-drag starts a window when it begins on an object, plus lasso selection by press-and-drag. PICKDRAG decides whether a window needs two clicks or click-and-drag. Together they define the feel of selection and are the first things to check when users report 'I cannot window select'.
tools.usage:
PICKAUTO = bit sum: 0 no automatic window | 1 window/crossing when clicking empty space (default) | 2 start a window even when starting on an object (with drag) | 4 lasso (press and drag)  - default 5
PICKDRAG = 0 two clicks for a window | 1 click-and-drag | 2 both (default)
OPTIONS > Selection: Implied windowing, Object grouping, Associative hatch, Allow press and drag on object, Allow press and drag for Lasso

parameters.name: lasso
parameters.description: Press-and-drag in empty space draws a freeform lasso; Spacebar cycles Window/Crossing/Fence lasso.

parameters.name: PICKFIRST
parameters.description: 1 allows selecting before issuing a command (noun-verb).

tools.example:
PICKAUTO 1
PICKDRAG 2
tools.notes: Registry settings. SELECTIONOFFSCREEN (2018+) additionally allows window selections to include objects off screen.

tools.name: SELECTIONCYCLING
tools.description: Enables selection cycling for overlapping objects: when several objects lie under the pick point a badge appears and, with the list mode, a small list box shows the candidates so the right one can be chosen. 0 off, 1 badge only, 2 badge plus list (default). The status-bar Selection Cycling button toggles it and DSETTINGS > Selection Cycling sets the list position and appearance. Shift+Space still cycles through candidates the old way.
tools.usage:
SELECTIONCYCLING = 0 off | 1 badge, cycle with Shift+Space | 2 badge and list box (default)
DSETTINGS > Selection Cycling tab: Allow selection cycling, Display selection cycling list box, Cursor-dependent / Static, Quadrant, Distance in pixels, Show title bar

parameters.name: Ctrl+W
parameters.description: Toggles selection cycling.

parameters.name: Shift+Space
parameters.description: Cycles through overlapping objects without the list.

tools.example:
SELECTIONCYCLING 2
(click on the overlapping wall lines; pick 'Polyline' from the list)
tools.notes: Registry setting. In 3D, Ctrl+click cycles sub-objects instead. The list only appears for objects within the pick box.

tools.name: SELECTIONPREVIEW
tools.description: Controls rollover highlighting: whether objects glow when the cursor passes over them with no command active (bit 1) or when a command prompts for selection (bit 2). SELECTIONAREA turns the translucent window/crossing fill on or off, WINDOWAREACOLOR/CROSSINGAREACOLOR/SELECTIONAREAOPACITY colour it, SELECTIONEFFECT chooses between the dashed-and-thickened legacy look (0) and the glow effect (1), SELECTIONEFFECTCOLOR sets the glow colour and PREVIEWFILTER excludes object types (xrefs, tables, groups, multiline text, hatches, locked layers) from the preview. All are in OPTIONS > Selection > Visual Effect Settings.
tools.usage:
SELECTIONPREVIEW = 0 off | 1 when no command is active | 2 when a command prompts for objects | 3 both (default)
SELECTIONAREA = 0 | 1 ; SELECTIONAREAOPACITY = 0-100 ; WINDOWAREACOLOR / CROSSINGAREACOLOR = ACI (defaults 150 / 100)
SELECTIONEFFECT = 0 legacy | 1 glow (default) ; SELECTIONEFFECTCOLOR = ACI (default 150 is not used; 'Default' means the highlight colour)
PREVIEWFILTER = bit sum: 1 xrefs, 2 tables, 4 groups, 8 multiline text, 16 hatches, 32 objects on locked layers (default 7)
SELECTIONPREVIEWLIMIT = max objects previewed during a window selection (default 2000)

parameters.name: performance
parameters.description: Rollover highlighting on huge drawings costs time; set SELECTIONPREVIEW 0 or raise PREVIEWFILTER bits to skip hatches and xrefs.

parameters.name: HIGHLIGHTSMOOTHING
parameters.description: Anti-aliasing of the highlight outline (hardware acceleration).

tools.example:
SELECTIONPREVIEW 2
PREVIEWFILTER 23
SELECTIONAREAOPACITY 15
tools.notes: All registry settings. The glow effect requires hardware acceleration; on software rendering the legacy effect is used regardless.

tools.name: PDSIZE
tools.description: Sets the display size of point objects: 0 means 5% of the viewport height (so points stay visible at any zoom), a positive value is an absolute size in drawing units, and a negative value is a percentage of the viewport height. It pairs with PDMODE (the point style) and both are set graphically with PTYPE; DIVIDE and MEASURE place point objects that are invisible unless PDMODE is changed from 0.
tools.usage:
PDSIZE = 0 (5% of viewport height, default) | >0 absolute units | <0 percentage of viewport height (e.g. -2)
PDMODE = 0 dot | 1 nothing | 2 plus | 3 cross | 4 vertical tick; add 32 circle, 64 square, 96 both
PTYPE  (Point Style dialog: icons for PDMODE; Set Size Relative to Screen / in Absolute Units)

parameters.name: REGEN
parameters.description: Point display changes take effect after a regeneration.

parameters.name: plot
parameters.description: Points plot at their displayed size; relative sizes depend on the plotted view.

tools.example:
PDMODE 34
PDSIZE -2
REGEN
tools.notes: Saved in the drawing. Survey imports with thousands of points are best shown with PDMODE 3 and a small relative size; nodes are snapped with the NOD object snap regardless of style.

tools.name: ANGDIR
tools.description: Sets the direction of positive angles - counterclockwise (0, default) or clockwise (1) - and ANGBASE the direction of angle 0 relative to the current UCS (default 0 = east). Both come from UNITS > Direction and affect angle entry, polar coordinates, DIMANGULAR text, ROTATE and every LISP function that reads angles (angle, polar) - but not the geometry stored in the database, which is always radians counterclockwise from the X axis.
tools.usage:
ANGDIR = 0 counterclockwise | 1 clockwise
ANGBASE = angle (in current AUNITS) of the zero direction, e.g. 90 for north-up bearings
UNITS > Clockwise checkbox / Direction... button

parameters.name: LISP
parameters.description: (angle p1 p2) returns radians ccw from the UCS X axis ignoring ANGDIR/ANGBASE; (angtos) and (angtof) honour them for display/parsing.

parameters.name: surveying
parameters.description: AUNITS 4 (surveyor's units) with ANGBASE 90 and ANGDIR 1 gives N 45 E style bearings.

tools.example:
ANGBASE 90
ANGDIR 1
ROTATE (select) 0,0 30   ; rotates 30 degrees clockwise from north
tools.notes: Saved in the drawing; drawings imported from GIS often carry these settings and confuse rotation prompts. Reset with UNITS before scripting geometry.

tools.name: LUPREC
tools.description: Number of decimal places (or the fraction denominator power for fractional units) displayed for linear values in the coordinate readout, LIST, DIST, Properties and default dimension text (through the dimension style's own precision when set to use it); AUPREC does the same for angles. They are the Precision fields of the UNITS dialog and only affect display, never the stored precision of coordinates.
tools.usage:
LUPREC = 0-8 (decimal places; for LUNITS 4/5 the denominator 1/2^n)
AUPREC = 0-8 (angle precision)
UNITS dialog > Length Precision / Angle Precision

parameters.name: LUNITS
parameters.description: 1 scientific, 2 decimal, 3 engineering, 4 architectural, 5 fractional.

parameters.name: DIMDEC / DIMADEC
parameters.description: Dimension style precision overrides LUPREC/AUPREC in dimension text.

parameters.name: rtos / angtos
parameters.description: LISP formatting functions default to LUNITS/LUPREC and AUNITS/AUPREC when their mode/precision arguments are omitted.

tools.example:
LUPREC 3
AUPREC 2
(rtos 12.34567) -> "12.346"
tools.notes: Saved in the drawing. A low LUPREC hides small errors in coordinates - use 8 when checking imported geometry.

tools.name: HPANG
tools.description: Default hatch pattern angle for the next HATCH (with HPNAME the pattern and HPSCALE the scale); HPTRANSPARENCY sets the default transparency (or Use Current/ByLayer), HPLAYER the default layer for new hatches ('.' = current), HPCOLOR the default hatch colour and HPBACKGROUNDCOLOR the background fill colour. These are the values the Hatch Creation ribbon tab shows and what -HATCH uses in scripts, so setting them first makes scripted hatching deterministic.
tools.usage:
HPANG = degrees (default 0)
HPSCALE = scale factor (default 1) ; HPNAME = pattern name or SOLID
HPTRANSPARENCY = 0-90 | "." use current (CETRANSPARENCY) | "ByLayer" | "ByBlock"
HPLAYER = layer name | "." (current)
HPCOLOR = colour | "." (current) ; HPBACKGROUNDCOLOR = colour | "." (none)

parameters.name: HPANNOTATIVE
parameters.description: 1 makes new hatches annotative.

parameters.name: HPINHERIT
parameters.description: 1 makes Inherit Properties copy the hatch origin as well as pattern/scale/angle.

parameters.name: HPRELATIVEPS
parameters.description: 1 scales hatches relative to paper space when created in a viewport.

tools.example:
HPNAME ANSI31
HPSCALE 25
HPANG 45
HPLAYER A-PATT
-HATCH
(pick internal point)
tools.notes: HPANG/HPSCALE/HPNAME are registry (session) values; HPLAYER/HPCOLOR/HPTRANSPARENCY are saved in the drawing. HATCH remembers the last used values into these variables, so scripts must set them explicitly.

tools.name: HPGAPTOL
tools.description: Gap tolerance for hatch boundary detection: gaps up to this distance (drawing units) between boundary objects are bridged so that nearly-closed areas can be hatched. Companion variables: HPASSOC (new hatches associative to their boundaries), HPISLANDDETECTION and HPISLANDDETECTIONMODE (Normal/Outer/Ignore islands and legacy vs. new algorithm), HPSEPARATE (one hatch object per closed area when picking several points), HPOBJWARNING (max boundary objects before a warning), HPDLGMODE (show the classic Hatch dialog instead of the ribbon tab) and HPPICKMODE (pick points vs. select objects default).
tools.usage:
HPGAPTOL = 0 (exact boundary required, default) .. 5000 drawing units
HPASSOC = 0 | 1 (default 1)
HPISLANDDETECTION = 0 Normal (alternate islands) | 1 Outer | 2 Ignore ; HPISLANDDETECTIONMODE = 0 legacy | 1 new (default)
HPSEPARATE = 0 one hatch for all picked areas | 1 separate hatch per area
HPOBJWARNING = number of boundary objects that triggers a warning (default 10000)
HPDLGMODE = 0 ribbon tab | 1 Hatch and Gradient dialog | 2 dialog only when the ribbon is off
HPPICKMODE = 0 pick internal point (default) | 1 select objects

parameters.name: HPGAPTOL pitfalls
parameters.description: Large tolerances let hatches leak through door openings; keep it small (e.g. 1-2 mm) and fix the linework instead.

parameters.name: HPMAXAREAS
parameters.description: Maximum number of enclosed areas a single hatch may contain before it is displayed as solid for performance.

tools.example:
HPGAPTOL 2
HPASSOC 1
HPISLANDDETECTION 1
HATCH (pick inside the room with the small gap)
tools.notes: HPGAPTOL, HPASSOC and HPSEPARATE are registry values; HPISLANDDETECTION is saved per drawing. A gap larger than the tolerance gives 'Hatch boundary not found' with red circles marking the gaps (HPQUICKPREVIEW shows the fill before committing).

tools.name: CETRANSPARENCY
tools.description: Current transparency level for new objects: ByLayer (default), ByBlock or 0-90 percent, set with the TRANSPARENCY control in the Properties panel of the ribbon. Transparency is a per-object/per-layer property like colour; it displays when TRANSPARENCYDISPLAY is 1 and plots only when 'Plot transparency' is checked in the plot dialog (PLOTTRANSPARENCYOVERRIDE), because transparent plots are rasterised and slow.
tools.usage:
CETRANSPARENCY = "ByLayer" | "ByBlock" | 0-90
TRANSPARENCYDISPLAY = 0 | 1 (screen display of transparency)
PLOTTRANSPARENCYOVERRIDE = 0 never plot transparency | 1 use the Plot transparency checkbox (default) | 2 always plot transparency
Layer transparency: LAYER > Transparency column; hatch: HPTRANSPARENCY

parameters.description: Maximum; 100 would be invisible and is not allowed.

parameters.name: xrefs
parameters.description: XREF layer transparency is honoured; VISRETAINMODE bit 64 syncs it.

tools.example:
CETRANSPARENCY 50
HATCH ... (semi-transparent fill)
CETRANSPARENCY ByLayer
tools.notes: Saved in the drawing. Transparency plotting to PDF via DWG To PDF works but produces large raster regions; use lighter colours or screening in the CTB for pen-plot workflows instead.

tools.name: CMLSTYLE
tools.description: Name of the current multiline style used by MLINE (defined with MLSTYLE), together with CMLJUST (justification of the multiline relative to its pick line: 0 top, 1 zero/centre, 2 bottom) and CMLSCALE (scale factor applied to the style's element offsets; negative flips the order). Setting these before MLINE in a script is equivalent to choosing the ST/J/S options at the MLINE prompt.
tools.usage:
CMLSTYLE = "STANDARD" | style name loaded from acad.mln or defined in the drawing
CMLJUST = 0 Top | 1 Zero | 2 Bottom
CMLSCALE = scale (default 1.0 metric / 20 imperial in some templates; negative mirrors the style)

parameters.name: MLSTYLE
parameters.description: Defines elements (offset, colour, linetype), caps, fill and joints; styles are saved in the drawing and in .mln files.

tools.example:
CMLSTYLE WALL-200
CMLJUST 1
CMLSCALE 1
MLINE 0,0 5000,0 5000,3000 (Enter)
tools.notes: Saved in the drawing. A style in use cannot be modified; MLINE objects are edited with MLEDIT and cannot be trimmed/filleted directly.

tools.name: CVPORT
tools.description: Identity number of the current viewport: 1 is paper space (the layout itself), 2 and up are model-space viewports (tiled in the Model tab, floating in layouts). Setting it makes another viewport current - the programmatic equivalent of clicking in it - and reading it tells LISP whether the user is in paper space. MAXACTVP limits how many viewports can display geometry at once (default 64), and VPMAXIMIZEDSTATE reports VPMAX.
tools.usage:
CVPORT = viewport id (1 = paper space; >=2 model space viewport; read the ids with (vports) in LISP or from the viewport entity's group 69)
MAXACTVP = 2-64 (default 64) active viewports per layout
TILEMODE = 1 Model tab | 0 layout

parameters.name: (vports)
parameters.description: LISP function returning ((id (llx lly) (urx ury)) ...) for the current tiled/floating viewports.

parameters.name: layout viewport entity
parameters.description: The VIEWPORT object's DXF group 69 is the id; group 68 status (0 off).

tools.example:
; LISP: activate the first floating viewport of the current layout
(if (= 1 (getvar "CVPORT"))
  (setvar "CVPORT" (car (cadr (vports)))))
; check for paper space
(if (= 1 (getvar "CVPORT")) (princ "\nPaper space is active."))
tools.notes: Setting CVPORT to an off or non-existent viewport errors. MSPACE/PSPACE are the command equivalents; in the Core Console CVPORT works for scripts that must set a viewport before ZOOM.

tools.name: DYNMODE
tools.description: Turns dynamic input on and controls its parts: pointer input (coordinates at the cursor), dimensional input (distance/angle fields while dragging) and dynamic prompts (command options at the cursor); DYNPROMPT shows the prompts, DYNPICOORDS decides whether typed coordinates are relative (0) or absolute (1) by default, DYNDIVIS how many dimension fields show, DYNTOOLTIPS whether tooltip appearance follows the OS, DYNINFOTIPS whether Shift/Ctrl hints appear, and DYNPIFORMAT polar vs Cartesian. F12 toggles it and DSETTINGS > Dynamic Input holds the same settings. With dynamic input on, typing 10,5 means relative @10,5 unless prefixed with # - the classic surprise for command-line users.
tools.usage:
DYNMODE = 0 off | 1 pointer input | 2 dimensional input | 3 both (default) | negative = off but remember
DYNPROMPT = 0 | 1 (show prompts at the cursor)
DYNPICOORDS = 0 relative (default) | 1 absolute  ; prefix # for absolute, @ for relative regardless
DYNPIFORMAT = 0 polar | 1 Cartesian
DYNDIVIS = 0 one field | 1 two | 2 all ; DYNTOOLTIPS = 0 | 1 ; DYNINFOTIPS = 0 | 1
DYNPIVIS = 0 show only on request (Down arrow) | 1 automatically when a point is requested | 2 always

parameters.name: Tab
parameters.description: Moves between the dimensional input fields; Down arrow opens the option list.

parameters.name: scripts
parameters.description: DYNMODE does not affect scripts or LISP (command input is parsed as absolute), only interactive typing.

tools.example:
DYNMODE 3
DYNPICOORDS 1   ; make typed coordinates absolute like the classic command line
tools.notes: Registry settings. Many long-time users run DYNMODE 0 with the command line docked; both styles are fully supported. Dynamic prompts are not shown for commands that lack them (LISP prompts appear only on the command line).

tools.name: TOOLTIPS
tools.description: Controls the display of tooltips on ribbon buttons, toolbars and palettes (TOOLTIPS 1) and their timing; ROLLOVERTIPS shows the object property tooltip when hovering geometry (the properties chosen in CUI > Rollover Tooltips), TOOLTIPMERGE combines drafting tooltips (osnap, polar, dynamic input) into one, and TOOLTIPSIZE / TOOLTIPTRANSPARENCY set their look. OPTIONS > Display > Show ToolTips / Show extended ToolTips / Show rollover ToolTips are the same settings.
tools.usage:
TOOLTIPS = 0 | 1
ROLLOVERTIPS = 0 | 1
TOOLTIPMERGE = 0 | 1
TOOLTIPSIZE = -3..6 ; TOOLTIPTRANSPARENCY = 0-100
OPTIONS > Display: Show ToolTips [Show shortcut keys in ToolTips, Show extended ToolTips, Number of seconds to delay], Show rollover ToolTips

parameters.name: extended tooltips
parameters.description: The second-level help image/text that appears after the delay on ribbon buttons.

parameters.name: AUTOSNAP bit 4
parameters.description: Object snap tooltips are controlled by AUTOSNAP, not TOOLTIPS.

tools.example:
ROLLOVERTIPS 0
TOOLTIPS 1
tools.notes: Registry settings. Rollover tooltips on very large drawings can lag; turning them off is a common performance tip.

tools.name: HIGHLIGHT
tools.description: Controls whether selected objects are highlighted (dashed/glowing) during a command's selection: 1 (default) on, 0 off. LISP routines set it to 0 while processing large selections to avoid the redraw cost, restoring it afterwards; it does not affect grips (GRIPS) or rollover preview (SELECTIONPREVIEW). HIGHLIGHTSMOOTHING anti-aliases the highlight when hardware acceleration is on.
tools.usage:
HIGHLIGHT = 0 no selection highlighting | 1 highlighting (default)
HIGHLIGHTSMOOTHING = 0 | 1

parameters.name: LISP pattern
parameters.description: (setq oh (getvar "HIGHLIGHT")) (setvar "HIGHLIGHT" 0) ... (setvar "HIGHLIGHT" oh) - with an *error* handler restoring it.

tools.example:
(setvar "HIGHLIGHT" 0)
(command "_.CHPROP" ss "" "_LA" "0" "")
(setvar "HIGHLIGHT" 1)
tools.notes: Saved in the drawing (not registry), so a routine that crashes with HIGHLIGHT 0 leaves that drawing without highlighting. sssetfirst can still show grips regardless.

tools.name: CURSORSIZE
tools.description: Size of the crosshair as a percentage of the screen (1-100; 100 gives full-screen crosshairs that old-school drafters use to line things up by eye). CURSORTYPE (2017+) chooses the pointer style, CURSORBADGE whether the cursor shows badges for the active tool/state, and OPTIONS > Display > Crosshair size is the same slider. Crosshair colour is set in OPTIONS > Display > Colors (Crosshairs element).
tools.usage:
CURSORSIZE = 1-100 (default 5)
CURSORTYPE = 0 arrow / crosshair per Windows | 1 large pointer
CURSORBADGE = 1 no badges | 2 badges shown (default)
tools.example:
CURSORSIZE 100
CURSORBADGE 1
tools.notes: Registry settings. Full-screen crosshairs slow down some graphics drivers slightly; harmless with hardware acceleration.

tools.name: PLINEGEN
tools.description: Sets how non-continuous linetypes are generated on new 2D polylines: 0 (default) restarts the pattern at each vertex, so short segments may show no dashes; 1 generates the pattern continuously across vertices. Related polyline variables: PLINETYPE (whether new polylines are lightweight LWPOLYLINE and whether old ones are converted on open), PLINEWID (default width for new polylines), PLINECONVERTMODE (how splines/fit curves become polylines - linear or arc segments) and PLINEREVERSEWIDTHS (behaviour of varying widths when REVERSE is run). Existing polylines are changed with PEDIT > Ltype gen or the Linetype generation property.
tools.usage:
PLINEGEN = 0 pattern per segment | 1 continuous pattern
PLINETYPE = 0 old-style POLYLINE, no conversion | 1 old-style kept, new are LWPOLYLINE | 2 (default) convert on open and create LWPOLYLINE
PLINEWID = default width (0)
PLINECONVERTMODE = 0 linear segments | 1 arc segments when converting splines (SPLINEDIT/PEDIT)
PLINEREVERSEWIDTHS = 0 widths stay with their vertices | 1 widths reversed with the direction

parameters.name: PEDIT L
parameters.description: Ltype gen ON/OFF on existing polylines.

parameters.name: LTGAPSELECTION
parameters.description: 1 allows picking/snapping in the gaps of dashed linetypes.

tools.example:
PLINEGEN 1
PLINE (draw a dashed centreline with many short segments) - the dashes flow continuously
tools.notes: PLINEGEN and PLINEWID are saved in the drawing; PLINETYPE and PLINECONVERTMODE are registry. Converted LWPOLYLINEs are lighter and faster; keep PLINETYPE 2 unless a legacy application needs old polylines.

tools.name: SPLFRAME
tools.description: Displays the control frame (polygon of control vertices) of splines and spline-fit polylines, and the invisible edges of 3D faces, when set to 1 - a diagnostic view for editing control points. The spline defaults live in SPLINETYPE (PEDIT spline curve type: 5 quadratic, 6 cubic B-spline), SPLINESEGS (segments per span for spline-fit polylines, negative for arc fitting), SPLMETHOD (0 fit points, 1 control vertices as the default for SPLINE), SPLKNOTS (knot parameterisation 0 chord, 1 square root, 2 uniform), SPLDEGREE (default degree 1-10 for CV splines) and SPLPERIODIC (periodic closed splines).
tools.usage:
SPLFRAME = 0 (default) | 1 show control frames and 3D face invisible edges
SPLINETYPE = 5 quadratic B-spline | 6 cubic B-spline (default)
SPLINESEGS = number of segments per spline-fit polyline segment (default 8; negative = arcs)
SPLMETHOD = 0 Fit | 1 Control Vertices ; SPLKNOTS = 0 chord | 1 square root | 2 uniform ; SPLDEGREE = 1-10 (default 3) ; SPLPERIODIC = 0 | 1

parameters.name: REGEN
parameters.description: SPLFRAME changes need a regeneration.

parameters.name: CVSHOW
parameters.description: The modern way to see and edit control vertices of splines and NURBS surfaces.

tools.example:
SPLFRAME 1
REGEN
(edit the control polygon with grips)
SPLFRAME 0
REGEN
tools.notes: All saved in the drawing except SPLMETHOD/SPLKNOTS/SPLDEGREE/SPLPERIODIC which are registry defaults for SPLINE. 3D face invisible edges are shown by SPLFRAME too, an old trick for editing PFACE meshes.

tools.name: EXPLMODE
tools.description: Allows EXPLODE to explode block references that were inserted with non-uniform scale factors (1, default) or refuses them (0), because non-uniformly scaled blocks explode into objects whose circles become ellipses and arcs become approximations. PEDITACCEPT is the neighbouring convenience: 1 lets PEDIT convert lines and arcs to polylines without asking 'Do you want to turn it into one?', which every polyline-editing script relies on.
tools.usage:
EXPLMODE = 0 refuse to explode non-uniformly scaled blocks | 1 explode them (default)
PEDITACCEPT = 0 ask before converting | 1 convert silently (default 0)

parameters.name: uniform scale check
parameters.description: A block with X=2, Y=1 is non-uniform; mirrored blocks (X=-1) are uniform in magnitude and explode normally.

tools.example:
PEDITACCEPT 1
PEDIT (select a line) J (select the arcs) Enter Enter  ; no confirmation prompt
tools.notes: EXPLMODE is registry; PEDITACCEPT is registry as well. Exploding a non-uniformly scaled block with circles gives ELLIPSE objects that some CAM tools reject.

tools.name: LAYLOCKFADECTL
tools.description: Fades the display of objects on locked layers by a percentage (0-90, default 50; negative stores the value while fading is off) so it is obvious what cannot be edited, without changing plots. The same slider is in the Layers ribbon panel (Locked Layer Fading). Locked-layer objects remain snappable and visible; they are simply not selectable for editing.
tools.usage:
LAYLOCKFADECTL = -90..90 (positive = fade percent; 0 no fade; negative = fading off, value remembered)
Ribbon: Home > Layers > Locked Layer Fading slider

parameters.name: plot
parameters.description: Fading is screen only; locked layers plot normally.

parameters.name: XDWGFADECTL
parameters.description: The equivalent for xrefs; XFADECTL for REFEDIT.

tools.example:
LAYLOCKFADECTL 70
LAYLCK (pick an object on the background layer)
tools.notes: Registry setting. Fading is applied after colour, so faded ByLayer colours look lighter but the CTB still maps their true ACI.

tools.name: GRIPS
tools.description: Controls grip display on selected objects: 0 none, 1 grips on (default), 2 grips plus midpoint grips on polyline segments (the extra grips that offer stretch/add vertex/convert to arc). The grip family also has GRIPSIZE (pixels), GRIPCOLOR / GRIPHOT / GRIPHOVER / GRIPCONTOUR (colours of unselected, selected, hovered grips and outline), GRIPBLOCK (grips on every object of a block reference instead of only the insertion point), GRIPMULTIFUNCTIONAL (Ctrl-cycling and hover menus on multifunctional grips), GRIPTIPS (grip tooltips for custom objects), GRIPOBJLIMIT (no grips when more than n objects are selected, default 100) and GRIPDYNCOLOR (dynamic block custom grips). OPTIONS > Selection > Grips holds all of them.
tools.usage:
GRIPS = 0 | 1 | 2 (default 2)
GRIPSIZE = 1-255 pixels (default 5) ; GRIPCOLOR = ACI (150) ; GRIPHOT = ACI (12) ; GRIPHOVER = ACI (11) ; GRIPCONTOUR = ACI (251)
GRIPBLOCK = 0 insertion point only | 1 all objects in the block
GRIPMULTIFUNCTIONAL = 0 off | 1 Ctrl cycling | 2 hover menu | 3 both (default)
GRIPOBJLIMIT = 0 always show | 1-32767 (default 100)
GRIPTIPS = 0 | 1 ; GRIPDYNCOLOR = ACI (140)

parameters.name: grip editing
parameters.description: Hover a grip for its menu; click it and press Space/Enter to cycle Stretch, Move, Rotate, Scale, Mirror; Ctrl+click to select several grips; Shift for copies.

parameters.name: GRIPOBJLIMIT
parameters.description: Raise it for scripts that use sssetfirst to show many grips, or lower it to speed up large selections.

tools.example:
GRIPSIZE 8
GRIPOBJLIMIT 500
GRIPBLOCK 0
tools.notes: All registry settings. Multifunctional grips are what make polylines, dimensions and multileaders editable without commands; GRIPS 1 disables the midpoint grips only.

tools.name: UCSFOLLOW
tools.description: When 1, changing the UCS in a viewport automatically switches that viewport to the plan view of the new UCS - handy in a dedicated 'plan' viewport, annoying elsewhere. The UCS family further includes UCSICON (icon on/off, at origin, properties; the command of the same name), UCSORTHO (orthographic view changes also set the matching UCS), UCSVIEW (a named view saves its UCS), UCSDETECT (dynamic UCS on 3D solid faces while drawing), UCSSELECTMODE (the UCS icon is selectable for grip editing), UCSNAME/UCSORG/UCSXDIR/UCSYDIR (read-only current UCS data), UCSBASE and WORLDVIEW (DVIEW/VPOINT operate relative to the WCS).
tools.usage:
UCSFOLLOW = 0 (default) | 1 (per viewport)
UCSICON = command: ON/OFF/All/Noorigin/ORigin/Selectable/Properties ; variable bits 1 on, 2 at origin
UCSORTHO = 0 | 1 (default 1) ; UCSVIEW = 0 | 1 (default 1) ; UCSDETECT = 0 | 1 (default 1, F6) ; UCSSELECTMODE = 0 | 1
WORLDVIEW = 0 | 1 (default 1)
Read-only: UCSNAME, UCSORG, UCSXDIR, UCSYDIR, WORLDUCS (1 when UCS = WCS)

parameters.name: UCSDETECT
parameters.description: Dynamic UCS: hovering a planar face of a solid during a draw command temporarily aligns the UCS to it (Shift+Z toggles).

parameters.name: UCSORTHO
parameters.description: With 1, choosing Front/Top from the ViewCube also sets the UCS to that plane so 2D commands draw on it.

tools.example:
UCSFOLLOW 1   ; in the plan viewport
UCS 3 (define a UCS on the sloped roof) -> the viewport shows the roof plan automatically
tools.notes: UCSFOLLOW, UCSICON and UCSORTHO are saved in the drawing (per viewport where applicable); UCSDETECT and UCSSELECTMODE are registry. LISP that transforms points should test WORLDUCS or use (trans ...) rather than assume the WCS.

tools.name: VIEWCTR
tools.description: Read-only centre of the current viewport's view in UCS coordinates; together with VIEWSIZE (height of the view in drawing units), VIEWDIR (viewing direction vector from target), VIEWTWIST (rotation of the view about the line of sight), VIEWMODE (perspective/clipping bits), VSMAX/VSMIN (virtual screen corners) and TARGET/LENSLENGTH, these describe the current view completely. LISP reads them to compute zoom windows, to save/restore views without VIEW, or to size text relative to the screen; they cannot be set directly - use ZOOM, VIEW, DVIEW or (vla-put-Center/Height on the viewport).
tools.usage:
VIEWCTR = (x y z) read-only ; VIEWSIZE = real read-only ; VIEWDIR = (x y z) read-only ; VIEWTWIST = angle read-only
VIEWMODE = bit sum read-only: 1 perspective, 2 front clipping, 4 back clipping, 8 UCS follow, 16 front clip not at eye
VSMAX / VSMIN = upper-right / lower-left of the virtual screen (read-only)
SCREENSIZE = (width height) of the viewport in pixels (read-only)

parameters.name: pixel size
parameters.description: (/ (getvar "VIEWSIZE") (cadr (getvar "SCREENSIZE"))) gives drawing units per pixel - the basis for screen-relative sizes.

parameters.name: restore a view
parameters.description: (command "_.ZOOM" "_C" ctr size) reproduces a saved VIEWCTR/VIEWSIZE.

tools.example:
; LISP: draw a marker that is always 20 pixels tall
(setq h (* 20 (/ (getvar "VIEWSIZE") (cadr (getvar "SCREENSIZE")))))
(command "_.CIRCLE" (getvar "VIEWCTR") (/ h 2))
tools.notes: Values refer to the current viewport (CVPORT). VIEWTWIST affects how DVIEW-rotated plans read: text drawn at angle 0 appears rotated on screen by the twist.

tools.name: SNAPMODE
tools.description: Turns grid snap on (1) or off (0) for the current viewport (F9) and is the head of the snap family: SNAPUNIT (X and Y snap spacing), SNAPBASE (origin of the snap and hatch grid), SNAPANG (rotation of the snap/grid/crosshair - the classic way to draft a rotated wing without changing the UCS), SNAPSTYL (0 rectangular, 1 isometric), SNAPISOPAIR (isometric plane: 0 left, 1 top, 2 right; F5 cycles) and SNAPTYPE (0 grid snap, 1 polar snap using POLARDIST). SNAPGRIDLEGACY makes the cursor snap only while a command is active. DSETTINGS > Snap and Grid exposes all of them.
tools.usage:
SNAPMODE = 0 | 1 (F9)
SNAPUNIT = (x y) e.g. 5,5 ; SNAPBASE = (x y) ; SNAPANG = degrees
SNAPSTYL = 0 standard | 1 isometric ; SNAPISOPAIR = 0 left | 1 top | 2 right (F5)
SNAPTYPE = 0 grid snap | 1 PolarSnap
SNAPGRIDLEGACY = 0 (snap always) | 1 (snap only when a point is requested)

parameters.name: ISODRAFT
parameters.description: 2015+ command/status-bar toggle that sets SNAPSTYL 1 and the isoplane in one go.

parameters.name: SNAPANG and hatch
parameters.description: SNAPANG also rotates hatch patterns' base angle in older releases; HPORIGIN/HPANG are the modern controls.

tools.example:
SNAPANG 30
SNAPUNIT 100,100
SNAPMODE 1
(draft the rotated wing; ORTHO follows the rotated crosshair)
tools.notes: All saved in the drawing per viewport. Scripts that pick points with snap on may land off-target; set SNAPMODE 0 first. Object snaps (OSMODE) are independent of grid snap.

tools.name: GRIDMODE
tools.description: Turns the grid display on (1) or off (0) for the current viewport (F7); GRIDUNIT sets the X/Y spacing (0 = follow SNAPUNIT), GRIDSTYLE switches between the lined grid (0) and the classic dotted grid (bits 1 2D model space, 2 Block Editor, 4 layouts), GRIDDISPLAY controls whether the grid is restricted to the limits, adapts its density when zoomed and follows the dynamic UCS, and GRIDMAJOR sets how many minor lines lie between major lines. The grid is display-only and never plots.
tools.usage:
GRIDMODE = 0 | 1 (F7)
GRIDUNIT = (x y) (0,0 = same as SNAPUNIT)
GRIDSTYLE = bit sum: 0 lines everywhere | 1 dots in 2D model space | 2 dots in the Block Editor | 4 dots in layouts
GRIDDISPLAY = bit sum: 0 grid within LIMITS only | 1 grid beyond limits (default) | 2 adaptive grid | 4 allow subdivision below grid spacing | 8 follow dynamic UCS
GRIDMAJOR = 1-100 minor lines per major line (default 5)

parameters.name: LIMITS
parameters.description: With GRIDDISPLAY bit 1 off, the grid marks the drawing limits - the old way of seeing the sheet area in model space.

tools.example:
GRIDUNIT 10,10
GRIDMAJOR 10
GRIDDISPLAY 7
GRIDMODE 1
tools.notes: Saved in the drawing per viewport. A grid too dense for the zoom level is suppressed with 'Grid too dense to display' unless adaptive grid is on.

tools.name: POLARMODE
tools.description: Bit-coded settings of polar tracking and object snap tracking: measure polar angles absolutely or relative to the last segment, track orthogonally only or at polar angles, acquire tracking points automatically or with Shift, and display the polar tooltip; POLARANG sets the polar increment angle, POLARADDANG a list of extra angles, POLARDIST the PolarSnap distance (SNAPTYPE 1), and AUTOSNAP bits 8/16/32 turn polar tracking, object snap tracking and their tooltips on. F10 toggles polar tracking; DSETTINGS > Polar Tracking holds the dialog.
tools.usage:
POLARMODE = bit sum: 1 measure polar angles relative to the last segment (0 = absolute to the UCS) | 2 use polar tracking angles in object snap tracking (0 = track orthogonally only) | 4 use additional polar tracking angles (POLARADDANG) | 8 acquire object snap tracking points only while Shift is held (0 = acquire automatically) - default 0
POLARANG = increment angle (default 90; typical 45, 30, 15)
POLARADDANG = "22.5;67.5" additional angles (up to 10, absolute)
POLARDIST = PolarSnap distance
AUTOSNAP bit 8 = polar tracking on (F10), bit 16 = object snap tracking on (F11), bit 32 = tooltips

parameters.name: relative angles
parameters.description: Bit 1 makes the next polar angle measure from the last drawn segment - useful for chained angled walls.

parameters.name: ORTHOMODE
parameters.description: Ortho and polar are mutually exclusive: turning one on turns the other off.

tools.example:
POLARANG 15
POLARADDANG 22.5;67.5
POLARMODE 4
AUTOSNAP 63
tools.notes: All registry settings except none saved in drawing; check the help for exact bit meanings in the current release since bit 16 semantics changed historically. Polar tracking is the accurate replacement for ORTHO when drafting at fixed angles.

tools.name: AUTOSNAP
tools.description: Bit-coded control of the AutoSnap aids: marker (1), magnet (2), tooltip (4), polar tracking (8), object snap tracking (16), tracking tooltip (32) - default 63. Its neighbours refine snapping: OSNAPZ (1 projects snapped points onto the current elevation instead of taking their true Z - essential for 2D work over 3D data), 3DOSMODE (3D object snaps: vertex, midpoint on edge, centre of face, knot, perpendicular, nearest to face, node), OSNAPCOORD (typed coordinates override running osnaps: 0 osnap wins, 1 keyboard wins, 2 keyboard wins except in scripts), OSOPTIONS (ignore hatches, ignore dynamic UCS Z, ignore negative Z), OSNAPNODELEGACY (Node snap on MTEXT insertion points) and TEMPOVERRIDES (temporary override keys such as Shift for ortho). OPTIONS > Drafting and DSETTINGS > Object Snap / 3D Object Snap are the dialogs.
tools.usage:
AUTOSNAP = bit sum: 1 marker | 2 magnet | 4 tooltip | 8 polar tracking | 16 object snap tracking | 32 tracking tooltip (default 63)
OSNAPZ = 0 use the snapped point's Z | 1 replace Z with the current ELEVATION
3DOSMODE = bit-coded set of 3D object snaps (vertex, midpoint on edge, centre of face, knot, perpendicular, nearest to face, node; 1 = none); set it from DSETTINGS > 3D Object Snap or F4 rather than by hand
OSNAPCOORD = 0 | 1 | 2 (default 2)
OSOPTIONS = bit sum: 1 ignore hatch objects | 2 ignore dynamic UCS Z | 4 ignore negative Z in dynamic UCS (default 3)
TEMPOVERRIDES = 0 | 1 (default 1)
OSNAPNODELEGACY = 0 Node snaps to MTEXT insertion | 1 legacy (ignores MTEXT)

parameters.name: OSNAPZ 1
parameters.description: Keeps 2D drafting flat when snapping to 3D solids, surveys or xrefs with elevations; set ELEVATION 0 as well.

parameters.name: OSNAPCOORD 2
parameters.description: Default: typed coordinates ignore running osnaps in interactive use but scripts' coordinates are still subject to osnaps - scripts should set OSMODE 0.

parameters.name: OSOPTIONS bit 1
parameters.description: Prevents snapping to hatch lines, a common cause of wrong endpoints.

tools.example:
OSNAPZ 1
ELEVATION 0
OSOPTIONS 3
AUTOSNAP 63
tools.notes: All registry settings except OSNAPZ (registry) and ELEVATION (drawing). Exact bit tables for 3DOSMODE differ slightly between releases; verify with the help before scripting. The Shift+right-click menu gives one-shot osnap overrides regardless of these settings.

tools.name: DRAGMODE
tools.description: Controls whether objects are shown dragging during MOVE/COPY/ROTATE/INSERT and similar commands: 0 never (no preview), 1 only when DRAG is typed at the prompt, 2 automatically (default). DRAGP1/DRAGP2 set the regen-drag and fast-drag input sampling rates, and BLIPMODE (0/1) draws the tiny + marks (blips) at picked points that older releases showed and REDRAW cleared. DRAGMODE 0 speeds up scripts that move thousands of objects interactively.
tools.usage:
DRAGMODE = 0 no dragging | 1 on request (type DRAG) | 2 automatic (default)
DRAGP1 = regen-drag input sampling rate (default 10) ; DRAGP2 = fast-drag sampling rate (default 25)
BLIPMODE = 0 (default) | 1 (blips at picked points)
DRAGVS = visual style used while dragging 3D solids ("" = current)

parameters.name: command preview
parameters.description: COMMANDPREVIEW (2015+) is the separate setting for previewing results of TRIM/EXTEND/OFFSET/FILLET before committing.

tools.example:
DRAGMODE 0
(command "_.MOVE" ss "" '(0 0) '(1000 0))
DRAGMODE 2
tools.notes: DRAGMODE is saved in the drawing; BLIPMODE is registry. Blips are purely visual and never plot; modern workflows leave them off.

tools.name: ELEVATION
tools.description: Current Z elevation, relative to the UCS, at which 2D objects are created when no Z is typed - and THICKNESS the extrusion height given to new 2D objects (lines, arcs, circles, polylines, text) so they become walls/fences in 3D. Both are set with the ELEV command or Properties. A non-zero ELEVATION left in a drawing is the classic reason new geometry 'floats' above the plan; OSNAPZ 1 makes snapped points respect it.
tools.usage:
ELEVATION = Z value (default 0)
THICKNESS = extrusion height (default 0)
ELEV  Specify new default elevation <0>: / Specify new default thickness <0>:

parameters.name: per-object
parameters.description: Elevation of an existing object is its Z (or the LWPOLYLINE Elevation property); Thickness is a property editable with CHPROP/Properties.

parameters.name: FLATTEN
parameters.description: Express Tool that resets Z of everything to 0 - the fix for floating geometry.

tools.example:
ELEVATION 0
THICKNESS 0
; check a drawing for floating objects: LIST a few, or use QSELECT with Elevation <> 0
tools.notes: Saved in the drawing (ELEVATION per space). Objects with thickness display as surfaces in shaded views and are treated as faces by HIDE.

tools.name: LWDISPLAY
tools.description: Shows lineweights on screen (1) or not (0, default) in the current drawing; the status-bar Lineweight button toggles it. LWDEFAULT sets the width that 'Default' lineweight means (default 0.25 mm = 25), LWUNITS whether lineweights are listed in millimetres (1) or inches (0), and the LWEIGHT dialog also has a display scale slider for model space. Lineweights always plot when 'Plot object lineweights' is on, whatever LWDISPLAY says.
tools.usage:
LWDISPLAY = 0 | 1 (per drawing; also per space in some releases)
LWDEFAULT = width in hundredths of mm (25 = 0.25 mm)
LWUNITS = 0 inches | 1 millimetres (default 1)
LWEIGHT dialog: Lineweights list, Units, Display Lineweight, Default, Adjust Display Scale

parameters.name: screen scale
parameters.description: In model space, displayed width is in pixels scaled by the slider, not by zoom; in layouts it is true to paper size.

parameters.name: 0.00 vs Default
parameters.description: A lineweight of 0.00 mm plots at the thinnest line the device can make; Default uses LWDEFAULT.

tools.example:
LWDISPLAY 1
LWDEFAULT 18
tools.notes: LWDISPLAY is saved in the drawing, LWDEFAULT/LWUNITS in the registry. CTB lineweights override object lineweights when the table assigns a width to the colour.

tools.name: 3DSELECTIONMODE
tools.description: Controls selection precedence of overlapping visually-styled 3D objects: 0 legacy (the topmost in draw order wins), 1 (default) the object closest to the viewer in shaded views. SUBOBJSELECTIONMODE sets the sub-object filter for Ctrl+click and the ribbon filter: 0 none, 1 vertices, 2 edges, 3 faces, 4 solid history, 5 drawing view components; DEFAULTGIZMO picks which gizmo appears for sub-object selections (move/rotate/scale/none) and GTAUTO whether it appears automatically. These decide how face/edge editing of solids and meshes feels.
tools.usage:
3DSELECTIONMODE = 0 | 1
SUBOBJSELECTIONMODE = 0 no filter | 1 vertex | 2 edge | 3 face | 4 solid history | 5 drawing view component
DEFAULTGIZMO = 0 move | 1 rotate | 2 scale | 3 none ; GTAUTO = 0 | 1 ; GTDEFAULT = 0 | 1 (3DMOVE/3DROTATE start with the gizmo)
GTLOCATION = 0 gizmo at the UCS origin | 1 at the selection centre

parameters.name: Ctrl+click
parameters.description: Selects sub-objects when SUBOBJSELECTIONMODE is 0; with a filter set, plain clicks select that sub-object type.

parameters.name: PRESSPULL / gizmo
parameters.description: Face selection plus the move gizmo is the interactive way to offset faces without SOLIDEDIT.

tools.example:
SUBOBJSELECTIONMODE 3
(click a face of the box; drag the gizmo's Z arrow 20 units)
SUBOBJSELECTIONMODE 0
tools.notes: All registry settings. Leaving SUBOBJSELECTIONMODE at 3 confuses 2D users because objects no longer select as wholes - reset it to 0 when done.

tools.name: ZOOMFACTOR
tools.description: Percentage change per mouse-wheel notch when zooming (3-100, default 60); ZOOMWHEEL reverses the wheel direction (0 forward = zoom in, 1 forward = zoom out), MBUTTONPAN makes the middle button pan (1, default) instead of opening the object-snap menu (0), and RTREGENAUTO (2021+) decides whether real-time zoom/pan regenerate automatically when the view leaves the generated area. VTENABLE/VTDURATION/VTFPS control smooth view transitions, and ZOOM's own behaviour is unaffected.
tools.usage:
ZOOMFACTOR = 3-100 (default 60)
ZOOMWHEEL = 0 (default) | 1 (reversed)
MBUTTONPAN = 0 (middle button = osnap menu) | 1 (pan; double-click = zoom extents)
RTREGENAUTO = 0 manual regen needed | 1 (default) automatic
VTENABLE = bit sum for smooth transitions (pan/zoom, view rotation, scripts); VTDURATION = ms; VTFPS = frames per second

parameters.name: Ctrl+wheel
parameters.description: Pans; Shift+wheel orbits in 3D (with the wheel button).

parameters.name: zoom limits
parameters.description: 'Already zoomed as far as possible' means a regen is needed (REGEN) when RTREGENAUTO is 0 or the drawing is huge.

tools.example:
ZOOMFACTOR 40
MBUTTONPAN 1
VTENABLE 0   ; disable smooth transitions for speed
tools.notes: All registry settings. Touch pads and 3D mice have their own settings in OPTIONS > System.

tools.name: SHORTCUTMENU
tools.description: Bit-coded control of right-click shortcut menus: 0 disables them entirely (right-click = Enter, the old behaviour many drafters prefer), 1 default menu when no objects are selected, 2 edit menu when objects are selected, 4 command menus while a command is active, 8 command menus only when options exist, 16 enable the time-sensitive right-click (short click = Enter, long click = menu; SHORTCUTMENUDURATION sets the threshold in ms). DBLCLKEDIT enables double-click editing (Properties or the in-place editor mapped in CUI > Double Click Actions). OPTIONS > User Preferences > Right-click Customization is the dialog.
tools.usage:
SHORTCUTMENU = bit sum: 0 none | 1 default menu | 2 edit menu | 4 command menu | 8 command menu only with options | 16 time-sensitive right-click  (default 11)
SHORTCUTMENUDURATION = 100-10000 ms (default 250)
DBLCLKEDIT = 0 | 1 (default 1)
OPTIONS > User Preferences > Windows Standard Behavior: Double click editing, Shortcut menus in drawing area, Right-click Customization...

parameters.name: time-sensitive
parameters.description: Bit 16 gives Enter on a quick click and the menu on a longer press - the compromise most CAD managers deploy.

tools.example:
SHORTCUTMENU 27   ; menus + time-sensitive right click
SHORTCUTMENUDURATION 300
tools.notes: Registry settings. Shortcut menu contents come from CUI > Shortcut Menus (Default Menu, Edit Menu, Command Menu, Object Snap Cursor Menu, object-specific menus by class name).

tools.name: FILLETRAD
tools.description: Current fillet radius used by FILLET (and FILLETEDGE for solids) - 0 produces a sharp corner, which is the classic trick for joining two lines exactly. The chamfer family holds CHAMFERA/CHAMFERB (first and second distances), CHAMFERC/CHAMFERD (length and angle) and CHAMMODE (0 distance-distance, 1 length-angle method); TRIMMODE decides whether FILLET/CHAMFER trim the original segments (1) or leave them (0), and FILLETPOLYARC (2019+) the fillet behaviour on polylines containing arcs. Scripts set these instead of answering the R/D options.
tools.usage:
FILLETRAD = radius (default 0)
CHAMFERA = dist1 ; CHAMFERB = dist2 ; CHAMFERC = length ; CHAMFERD = angle ; CHAMMODE = 0 | 1
TRIMMODE = 0 no trim | 1 trim (default)
FILLETPOLYARC = 0 current behaviour | 1 legacy

parameters.name: FILLET with radius 0
parameters.description: Extends/trims two lines to meet; Shift+click in FILLET does the same for one corner without changing FILLETRAD.

parameters.name: Polyline option
parameters.description: FILLET P fillets every vertex of a polyline at FILLETRAD.

tools.example:
FILLETRAD 5
FILLET (pick two lines)
; script
FILLETRAD 0
FILLET P (select the polyline)   ; cleans all corners sharp
tools.notes: FILLETRAD, CHAMFER* and TRIMMODE are saved in the drawing. TRIMMODE 0 is occasionally left on by routines and makes FILLET appear broken - check it first.

tools.name: OFFSETDIST
tools.description: Default offset distance for OFFSET (negative = Through mode); OFFSETGAPTYPE controls how gaps at the corners of offset polylines are closed (0 extend segments to a sharp corner, 1 fillet with the offset distance, 2 chamfer) and OFFSETLAYER? - no: the Layer option of OFFSET (current/source) is remembered in the command, not a variable. Set OFFSETDIST before scripted OFFSET so the default prompt can be accepted with Enter.
tools.usage:
OFFSETDIST = distance (default -1 = Through)
OFFSETGAPTYPE = 0 sharp corners (default) | 1 filleted | 2 chamfered
OFFSET  Specify offset distance or [Through/Erase/Layer] <OFFSETDIST>:

parameters.name: Erase option
parameters.description: OFFSET E Y deletes the source after offsetting (remembered for the session).

parameters.name: Layer option
parameters.description: OFFSET L C puts offsets on the current layer instead of the source layer.

tools.example:
OFFSETDIST 250
OFFSETGAPTYPE 1
OFFSET

(pick the polyline) (pick the side)
tools.notes: OFFSETDIST is saved in the drawing; OFFSETGAPTYPE is registry. Offsetting splines/ellipses creates splines; offsetting a polyline with arcs of radius smaller than the offset drops those segments.

tools.name: MIRRHATCH
tools.description: Controls whether hatch patterns are mirrored with their boundaries by MIRROR (1) or keep their original angle (0, default, since 2015) - the hatch equivalent of MIRRTEXT. The editing-default family also includes EDGEMODE (TRIM/EXTEND use implied extensions of the cutting/boundary edges when 1), PROJMODE (0 true 3D, 1 project to the UCS, 2 project to the view for TRIM/EXTEND of 3D geometry) and TRIMEXTENDMODE/TRIMEDGES (2021+, Quick mode defaults and whether hatch pattern lines act as edges).
tools.usage:
MIRRHATCH = 0 hatch angle retained | 1 hatch mirrored
MIRRTEXT = 0 text readable | 1 text mirrored
EDGEMODE = 0 real edges only | 1 implied (extended) edges
PROJMODE = 0 true 3D | 1 UCS plane (default) | 2 current view
TRIMEXTENDMODE = 0 Standard mode | 1 Quick mode (default) ; TRIMEDGES = 0 hatch boundary only | 1 hatch pattern lines act as edges

parameters.name: Quick mode
parameters.description: TRIM/EXTEND select all objects as edges automatically and trim by clicking or dragging a fence; Standard mode asks for edges first (TRIM O Enter).

tools.example:
MIRRHATCH 0
MIRRTEXT 0
EDGEMODE 1
TRIMEXTENDMODE 0   ; classic TRIM prompts for scripts
tools.notes: MIRRHATCH, MIRRTEXT, EDGEMODE and PROJMODE are saved in the drawing; TRIMEXTENDMODE is registry. Scripts written for the classic TRIM must set TRIMEXTENDMODE 0 or use the mOde option.

tools.name: WINDOWAREACOLOR
tools.description: Colour of the translucent fill of a window selection (default ACI 150, blue) and CROSSINGAREACOLOR of a crossing selection (default 100, green), with SELECTIONAREAOPACITY for the transparency and SELECTIONAREA to turn the fill off; in 2014+ the lasso and fence selections share them. Changing the colours helps users with colour-vision deficiency and screen recordings; they are in OPTIONS > Selection > Visual Effect Settings.
tools.usage:
WINDOWAREACOLOR = 1-255 (default 150)
CROSSINGAREACOLOR = 1-255 (default 100)
SELECTIONAREAOPACITY = 0-100 (default 25)
SELECTIONAREA = 0 | 1
tools.example:
WINDOWAREACOLOR 5
CROSSINGAREACOLOR 2
SELECTIONAREAOPACITY 40
tools.notes: Registry settings. The dashed outline of crossing windows is drawn regardless of the fill.

tools.name: MAXSORT
tools.description: Maximum number of symbol names (layers, blocks, styles) that list commands and dialogs sort alphabetically (default 1000; 0-32767); above the limit lists appear in creation order, which looks like a bug in drawings with thousands of layers. SORTORDER (2015+) chooses natural sort (1: Layer2 before Layer10) or ASCII sort (0) for the layer list. Both are registry settings that CAD managers raise for large projects.
tools.usage:
MAXSORT = 0-32767 (default 1000)
SORTORDER = 0 ASCII | 1 natural (default 1)
tools.example:
MAXSORT 10000
SORTORDER 1
tools.notes: Sorting many thousands of names slows the Layer Properties Manager; MAXSORT is the trade-off. LISP (tblnext) enumerates in table order, unaffected.
